title: London vs Paris: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: London for free museums, language ease, food diversity, and pub culture. Paris for iconic sights, romance, walkability, and French cuisine. Do both if you have 7+ days.

categories.name: Food & Dining
categories.summary: London wins on global diversity; Paris wins on French cuisine and bistro culture.

categories.name: Culture & Museums
categories.summary: London has free world-class museums; Paris has more iconic paid attractions.

categories.name: Cost
categories.summary: London 15-20% pricier on accommodation; Paris costs more on attraction entry.

categories.name: Getting Around
categories.summary: Paris Metro is cheaper and city is more walkable. London Tube is excellent but pricier.

categories.name: Best Time to Visit
categories.summary: May, June, September ideal for both. London works well in winter too.

categories.name: Nightlife
categories.summary: London pubs and 24-hour weekend Tube beat Paris for nightlife.

categories.name: Romance
categories.summary: Paris is unmatched for romance — Seine sunsets, Montmartre, café culture.

categories.name: Day Trips
categories.summary: Different but equal: Bath/Oxford vs Versailles/Giverny.

categories.name: Safety
categories.summary: Both safe; London has stronger bystander culture and easier navigation.

faq.question: Is London or Paris better for first-time visitors?
faq.answer: London for English speakers wanting ease; Paris for bucket-list European experience. Ideally do both via Eurostar.

faq.question: How far apart are London and Paris?
faq.answer: 340km, 2h15m by Eurostar from £39 booked in advance.

faq.question: Is London more expensive than Paris?
faq.answer: London 15-20% pricier on accommodation, but Paris charges €15-22 per museum while London museums are free. Overall similar.
